# `PIXterm` - *draw images in your ANSI terminal with true color*

**`PIXterm`** ***shows images directly in your terminal***, recreating the pixels through a combination of [ANSI character background color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Colors) and the [unicode lower half block element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements). If image has transparency, an optional matte color can be used for background. Also, you can specify a dithering mode; in which case, the image is rendered using block elements with different shades, or using standard ASCII characters in the same way. In dithering mode, the matte color is used to fill the background of the blocks or characters.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.

Fetching images from HTTP/HTTPS is supported too.

## Usage

```
pixterm [options] <image file or URL>
```

### Options

- `-version` - show PIXterm version
- `-credits` - show some love to contributors <3
- `-d <mode>` - dithering mode:
  - `0` - no dithering (default)
  - `1` - with blocks
  - `2` - with chars
- `-go` - output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image
- `-m <color>` - matte color for transparency or background (optional, hex format, default: 000000)
- `-nobg` - disable background color (optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)
- `-s <method>` - scale method:
  - `0` - resize (default)
  - `1` - fill
  - `2` - fit
- `-tr <rows>` - terminal rows (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)
- `-tc <columns>` - terminal columns (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)

# `PIXterm` - *draw images in your ANSI terminal with true color*

**`PIXterm`** ***shows images directly in your terminal***, recreating the pixels through a combination of [ANSI character background color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Colors) and the [unicode lower half block element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements). If image has transparency, an optional matte color can be used for background. Also, you can specify a dithering mode; in which case, the image is rendered using block elements with different shades, or using standard ASCII characters in the same way. In dithering mode, the matte color is used to fill the background of the blocks or characters.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.

Fetching images from HTTP/HTTPS is supported too.

## Usage

```
pixterm [options] <image file or URL>
```

### Options

- `-version` - show PIXterm version
- `-credits` - show some love to contributors <3
- `-d <mode>` - dithering mode:
  - `0` - no dithering (default)
  - `1` - with blocks
  - `2` - with chars
- `-go` - output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image
- `-m <color>` - matte color for transparency or background (optional, hex format, default: 000000)
- `-nobg` - disable background color (optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)
- `-s <method>` - scale method:
  - `0` - resize (default)
  - `1` - fill
  - `2` - fit
- `-tr <rows>` - terminal rows (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)
- `-tc <columns>` - terminal columns (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)

## Screenshots

### Cool Screenshots

![Screenshot 1](docs/images/screenshot01.png)

#### No Dithering (Classic Mode)

![Screenshot 2](docs/images/screenshot02.png)

![Screenshot 3](docs/images/screenshot03.png)

![Screenshot 4](docs/images/screenshot04.png)

![Screenshot 5](docs/images/screenshot05.png)

![Screenshot 6](docs/images/screenshot06.png)

#### Dithering with Blocks

![Screenshot 7](docs/images/screenshot07.png)

![Screenshot 8](docs/images/screenshot08.png)

![Screenshot 9](docs/images/screenshot09.png)

#### Dithering with Characters

![Screenshot 10](docs/images/screenshot10.png)

![Screenshot 11](docs/images/screenshot11.png)

![Screenshot 12](docs/images/screenshot12.png)

#### Dithering with Background Color Disabled (`-nobg`)

![Screenshot 13](docs/images/screenshot13.png)

![Screenshot 14](docs/images/screenshot14.png)

## Requirements

Your terminal emulator must support *true color* in order to display image colors correctly. In addition, you must use a monospaced font that includes the lower half block unicode character: `▄ (U+2584)`. [Envy Code R](https://damieng.com/blog/2008/05/26/envy-code-r-preview-7-coding-font-released) is recommended. If you want to use the dithering mode with blocks, the font must also include the following unicode characters: `█ (U+2588)`, `▓ (U+2593)`, `▒ (U+2592)`, `░ (U+2591)`. The dithering mode with characters works with standard ASCII chars.

import zlib, struct
def chunk(t,data):
    return struct.pack(">I",len(data))+t+data+struct.pack(">I",zlib.crc32(t+data)&0xffffffff)
def solid_png(path,w,h,rgb=(200,100,50)):
    row=b"\x00"+bytes(rgb)*w
    raw=row*h
    ihdr=struct.pack(">IIBBBBB",w,h,8,2,0,0,0)
    open(path,"wb").write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"+chunk(b"IHDR",ihdr)+chunk(b"IDAT",zlib.compress(raw,1))+chunk(b"IEND",b""))
def grad_png(path,w,h):
    # R depends on y scaled 0-255, G on x scaled, B=100 ; use RGB
    rows=[]
    # precompute G line template per x as bytes
    # row bytes varying R per row so need construct each row using bytearray stepping maybe use memory?
    # use arrays: for each y, row bytearray of w*3
    raw=bytearray()
    gvals=[(x*255//max(w-1,1)) for x in range(w)]
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        r=(y*255//max(h-1,1))
        # interleave: use bytearray and slice assign
        row=bytearray(w*3)
        row[0::3]=bytes([r])*w
        row[1::3]=bytes(gvals)
        row[2::3]=b'\x64'*w
        raw.extend(row)
    ihdr=struct.pack(">IIBBBBB",w,h,8,2,0,0,0)
    open(path,"wb").write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"+chunk(b"IHDR",ihdr)+chunk(b"IDAT",zlib.compress(bytes(raw),1))+chunk(b"IEND",b""))

import math
def lanczos(x,a=3):
    if x==0: return 1
    if abs(x)>=a: return 0
    return (math.sin(math.pi*x)/(math.pi*x))*(math.sin(math.pi*x/a)/(math.pi*x/a))
def weights(src,dst, support_filter=3, kernel=lanczos):
    scale=src/dst
    support=support_filter*scale if scale>1 else support_filter
    out=[]
    for d in range(dst):
        fx=(d+0.5)*scale
        start=max(0, int(fx-support+0.5) if False else math.floor(fx-support))
        # variants
        vals=[]
        s=0
        for i in range(src):
            # centre of src i is i+0.5, distance fx-(i+0.5)
            dist=(fx-(i+0.5))
            scaled=dist/scale if scale>1 else dist

import os, pty, fcntl, termios, struct, subprocess, select, sys, time

def run_pty(args, rows, cols):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    # set winsize on slave (and master)
    winsize = struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    fcntl.ioctl(master, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    p=subprocess.Popen(["/workspace/executable"]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    out=b""
    while True:
        rl,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],2)
        if not rl: break
        try:
            data=os.read(master,65536)
        except OSError:
            break
        if not data:break
        out+=data
        if p.poll() is not None:
            # drain briefly
            pass
    try:p.wait(timeout=2)

    # tty translates \n to \r\n; count lines by \r\n or \n

    kw={}

    p=subprocess.Popen(["/workspace/executable"]+args,close_fds=True,**kw)

    os.close(slave)

        while True:

import struct
def write_tiff(path,w,h,pixels,samples=3,bits=8):
    # little endian, one strip, RGB
    data=b''.join(bytes(p[:samples]) for row in pixels for p in row)
    # header 8, IFD after data? Put IFD at 8, then extra values, then strip.
    # We'll construct entries sorted by tag.
    # Tags: 256 width,257 height,258 bits (3 shorts),259 compression1,262 photometric2,273 strip offset,277 spp,278 rows/strip=h,279 strip byte counts,284 planar1
    n=10
    ifd_offset=8
    ifd_size=2+n*12+4
    extra_offset=ifd_offset+ifd_size
    strip_offset=extra_offset+6  # bits array 3 shorts
    def e(tag,typ,count,val):
        return struct.pack('<HHI',tag,typ,count)+val
    def shortval(v): return struct.pack('<H',v)+b'\x00\x00'
    def longval(v): return struct.pack('<I',v)
    entries=b''
    entries+=e(256,4,1,longval(w));entries+=e(257,4,1,longval(h));entries+=e(258,3,3,longval(extra_offset));entries+=e(259,3,1,shortval(1));entries+=e(262,3,1,shortval(2));entries+=e(273,4,1,longval(strip_offset));entries+=e(277,3,1,shortval(samples));entries+=e(278,4,1,longval(h));entries+=e(279,4,1,longval(len(data)));entries+=e(284,3,1,shortval(1))
    out=b'II*\x00'+struct.pack('<I',ifd_offset)+struct.pack('<H',n)+entries+struct.pack('<I',0)+struct.pack('<HHH',bits,bits,bits)+data
    open(path,'wb').write(out)

import sys,math,subprocess,re,random
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/work')
from gen import write_png
from candidate import resize_pass

def binary(img,tc,tr):
    write_png('/tmp/work/tmp.png',len(img[0]),len(img),img,6)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable.orig','-s','1','-tc',str(tc),'-tr',str(tr),'/tmp/work/tmp.png'],capture_output=True)
    rows=[]
    for line in r.stdout.decode().splitlines():
        seq=[tuple(map(int,v.split(';'))) for v in re.findall(r'\[(?:48|38);2;(\d+;\d+;\d+)m',line)];rows.append(seq[0::2]);rows.append(seq[1::2])
    return rows

def crop(img,x,y,w,h):return [row[x:x+w] for row in img[y:y+h]]
def score(exp,stage):
    cand=stage[2:];diff=sum(1 for y in range(len(exp)) for x in range(len(exp[0])) for c in range(3) if exp[y][x][c]!=cand[y][x][c]);mae=sum(abs(exp[y][x][c]-cand[y][x][c]) for y in range(len(exp)) for x in range(len(exp[0])) for c in range(3))/(len(exp)*len(exp[0])*3);return diff,round(mae,3)
def rc(img,tw,th):
    W=len(img[0]);H=len(img)
    if W*th>H*tw: iw=int(W*th/H+0.5);ih=th
    else: iw=tw;ih=int(H*tw/W+0.5)
    resized=resize_pass(img,iw,ih);return crop(resized,(iw-tw)//2,(ih-th)//2,tw,th)
def cr(img,tw,th,mode='round'):
    W=len(img[0]);H=len(img)
    conv=lambda v:int(v+0.5) if mode=='round' else int(v) if mode=='floor' else math.ceil(v)
    if W*th>H*tw: cw=conv(H*tw/th);ch=H
    else: cw=W;ch=conv(W*th/tw)
    return resize_pass(crop(img,(W-cw)//2,(H-ch)//2,cw,ch),tw,th)

import os,pty,fcntl,termios,struct,subprocess,select,re
def capture(exe,args,rows=24,cols=80):
    m,s=pty.openpty();fcntl.ioctl(s,termios.TIOCSWINSZ,struct.pack('HHHH',rows,cols,0,0));attrs=termios.tcgetattr(s);attrs[1]&=~termios.OPOST;termios.tcsetattr(s,termios.TCSANOW,attrs)
    p=subprocess.Popen([exe]+args,stdout=s,stderr=s,stdin=s,close_fds=True);os.close(s);out=b''
    while True:
        rl,_,_=select.select([m],[],[],3)
        if not rl:break
        try:d=os.read(m,65536)
        except OSError:break
        if not d:break
        out+=d
    p.wait();os.close(m);return p.returncode,out
def norm(b):return re.sub(rb'\d{4}/\d\d/\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d',b'TIME',b)
def compare(args,rows=24,cols=80):
    a=capture('/workspace/executable.orig',args,rows,cols);b=capture('/tmp/candbin/executable',args,rows,cols)
    ok=a[0]==b[0] and norm(a[1])==norm(b[1])
    print(args,rows,cols,'match',ok,'exits/lens',a[0],b[0],len(a[1]),len(b[1]))
    if not ok:
        x,y=a[1],b[1]
        for i in range(min(len(x),len(y))):
            if x[i]!=y[i]:print(' diff',i,repr(x[max(0,i-50):i+100]),repr(y[max(0,i-50):i+100]));break
    return ok

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# WebP decoding uses the system libwebp through cgo. If it (or a C
# compiler) is unavailable, fall back to a build without WebP support
# rather than failing the whole build.
TAGS=""
if command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1 && { [ -e /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwebp.so.7 ] || ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libwebp\.so'; }; then
	export CGO_ENABLED=1
else
	if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		(apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq gcc libwebp7) >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
	fi
	if command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1 && { [ -e /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwebp.so.7 ] || ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libwebp\.so'; }; then
		export CGO_ENABLED=1
	else
		export CGO_ENABLED=0
		TAGS="-tags nowebp"
	fi
fi

if [ -n "${TAGS}" ]; then
	go build -trimpath ${TAGS} -o executable .
elif GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.11 go version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.11 go build -trimpath -o executable .
else
	go build -trimpath -o executable .
fi

package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"image/color"
	"io"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func printUsage(fs *flag.FlagSet) {
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, plainLogo)
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "USAGE:\n\n  %s [options] image/url\n\n  Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.\n  Supported URL protocols: HTTP, HTTPS.\n\nOPTIONS:\n\n", filepath.Base(os.Args[0]))
	fs.SetOutput(os.Stdout)
	fs.PrintDefaults()
	fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, "  -help\n\tprints this message :D LOL\n\n")
}

func printLogo() {
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, plainLogo)
}

func fatalError(err error) {
	printLogo()
	log.Fatal(err)
}

func main() {
	log.SetPrefix("[PIXTERM ERROR] ")
	log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
	log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)

	fs := flag.NewFlagSet(os.Args[0], flag.ContinueOnError)
	fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)
	fs.Usage = func() { printUsage(fs) }

	showCredits := fs.Bool("credits", false, "show some love to contributors <3")
	dithering := fs.Int("d", 0, "dithering `mode`:\n   0 - no dithering (default)\n   1 - with blocks\n   2 - with chars")
	goMode := fs.Bool("go", false, "output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image")
	matteStr := fs.String("m", "", "matte `color` for transparency or background\n(optional, hex format, default: 000000)")
	noBG := fs.Bool("nobg", false, "disable background color\n(optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)")
	scaling := fs.Int("s", 0, "scale `method`:\n   0 - resize (default)\n   1 - fill\n   2 - fit")
	colsFlag := fs.Int("tc", 0, "terminal `columns` (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)")
	rowsFlag := fs.Int("tr", 0, "terminal `rows` (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)")
	showVersion := fs.Bool("version", false, "show PIXterm version")

	if err := fs.Parse(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
		if err == flag.ErrHelp {
			os.Exit(0)
		}
		os.Exit(2)
	}

	if *showVersion {
		fmt.Println("1.3.2")
		return
	}
	if *showCredits {
		if isTerminal(os.Stdout) {
			fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, fancyCredits)
		} else {
			printLogo()
			fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, contributorsText)
		}
		return
	}
	if fs.Arg(0) == "" || *dithering < 0 || *dithering > 2 || *scaling < 0 || *scaling > 2 || (*colsFlag != 0 && *colsFlag < 2) || (*rowsFlag != 0 && *rowsFlag < 2) {
		fs.Usage()

// toNRGBA converts any image to an 8-bit NRGBA image anchored at (0,0).
// It follows the behavior needed by the resizing code: source bounds
// offsets are honoured and the pixels are converted with the standard
// Go color model.
func toNRGBA(src image.Image) *image.NRGBA {
	if src == nil {
		return image.NewNRGBA(image.Rectangle{})
	}
	b := src.Bounds()
	w, h := b.Dx(), b.Dy()
	if w < 0 {
		w = 0
	}
	if h < 0 {
		h = 0
	}
	if n, ok := src.(*image.NRGBA); ok {
		if b.Min.X == 0 && b.Min.Y == 0 {
			out := *n
			out.Pix = append([]uint8(nil), n.Pix...)
			out.Rect = image.Rect(0, 0, w, h)
			return &out
		}
	}
	if rgba, ok := src.(*image.RGBA); ok {
		out := image.NewNRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, w, h))
		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				si := rgba.PixOffset(b.Min.X+x, b.Min.Y+y)
				di := y*out.Stride + x*4
				a := rgba.Pix[si+3]
				switch a {
				case 0:
					out.Pix[di+3] = 0
				case 255:
					copy(out.Pix[di:di+4], rgba.Pix[si:si+4])
				default:
					out.Pix[di+0] = uint8(uint32(rgba.Pix[si+0]) * 255 / uint32(a))
					out.Pix[di+1] = uint8(uint32(rgba.Pix[si+1]) * 255 / uint32(a))
					out.Pix[di+2] = uint8(uint32(rgba.Pix[si+2]) * 255 / uint32(a))

	// high byte of each channel. A draw through the standard colour

	// change some semi-transparent values by one.

				di := y*out.Stride + x*4

				out.Pix[di+1] = n64.Pix[si+2]

}
